test_title: RRB Technician Grade III Official Paper (Held On: 23 Dec, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Consider a long conducting wire carrying a current. Which of the following statements is NOT true?

options.text: The magnetic field will reverse the direction if we reverse the current.
We can use Fleming's left-hand rule to determine the direction of magnetic field.
The magnetic field decreases as we move away from the wire.
The strength of the magnetic field increases if we increase the current.

solution:
The correct answer is __**We can use Fleming's left-hand rule to determine the direction of magnetic field.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fleming's left-hand rule** is used to determine the direction of **force** experienced by a current-carrying conductor placed in a magnetic field, not the direction of the magnetic field.
 
• The correct rule to determine the direction of the magnetic field around a current-carrying conductor is the **Right-hand thumb rule**.
 
• According to the **Right-hand thumb rule**, if you grasp the conductor with your right hand such that the thumb points in the direction of the current, the fingers will curl around the conductor in the direction of the magnetic field lines.
 
• Reversing the current in the conductor will reverse the direction of the magnetic field lines around the conductor.
 
• The magnetic field strength decreases with increasing distance from the wire, following an inverse proportionality.
 
• Increasing the current in the wire will increase the strength of the magnetic field around the wire.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Right-hand thumb rule**__

 __
 
• This rule is specifically used to determine the direction of the **magnetic field** around a current-carrying conductor.
 
• It is also known as the **Maxwell's corkscrew rule**.
 
 
 
• **Magnetic field direction reversal**__
 __
 
• When the current in a conductor is reversed, the direction of the **magnetic field lines** around the conductor also reverses.
 
• This follows from the right-hand thumb rule.
 
 
 
• **Magnetic field strength and distance**__
 __
 
• The strength of the magnetic field around a current-carrying conductor **decreases with increasing distance** from the conductor.
 
• This is described by the equation B ∝ 1/r, where B is the magnetic field strength and r is the distance from the wire.
 
 
 
• **Increasing current and magnetic field strength**__
 
 
• Increasing the current in the wire will proportionally increase the **strength of the magnetic field** around the wire.
 
• This follows from the Biot-Savart law and Ampere's circuital law.
